title: USF Schema Registry
purpose: Defines the canonical schema system for USF: which JSON Schemas are expected, why each exists, what ontology concept it governs, what taxonomy classifications and vocabulary value sets it depends on, what authority level it supports, and what lifecycle state it is in. It governs later schema creation so future schemas do not drift in naming, identity, metadata, references, authority, or enum values. It is machine-readable governance, not a schema file. The registry artefact itself authors no schema files; the schema files it catalogues are now present under spec/schemas/ as separate artefacts (lifecycleState draft), validated against spec/schemas/schema-registry.schema.json.
normativeLanguage: Requirement words (MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, MAY) follow BCP 14 as defined in docs/architecture/standards-profile.md section 6. Only uppercase forms are normative.

identityNotes.isNotItselfASchemaFile: This registry is governance data; it is not a JSON Schema. Its validating schema spec/schemas/schema-registry.schema.json has now been authored (lifecycleState draft) and the registry is checked against it for shape; enforcement remains advisory until a validator tool is integrated (active).
identityNotes.idPrefixNote: This artefact uses the global artefact-ID namespace 'usf.' (id 'usf.schema-registry'), consistent with the taxonomy ('usf.taxonomy-catalog') and vocabulary ('usf.vocabulary-catalog') catalogues. The 'usf.' prefix is a deliberate globally-scoped machine-readable identifier namespace and is NOT a redundant-usf violation: the redundant-usf prohibition applies to repository path segments, package and implementation names, and unnecessary repeated local names, not to global artefact IDs that may be consumed outside the repository context. Schema file names and paths (e.g. spec/schemas/schema-registry.schema.json) remain unprefixed because they are paths, not global IDs.

taxonomyCatalogue.role: Classification authority (taxonomy). Source of schema family taxonomy alignment and classification references.

vocabularyCatalogue.role: Controlled-value authority (vocabulary). Source of schema classes, schema lifecycle states, authority levels, and all enum value sets schemas must reference.

schemaDirectory.note: Contains 23 authored schema files, one per registry entry, all lifecycleState draft. No schema is active: active promotion additionally requires a formal active/enforcing validator posture. The current validator exists as draft/advisory CI enforcement (tools/validate-spec/validate-spec.py) and does not promote schemas to active.

placeholderPolicy..gitkeep: A git placeholder to retain an empty directory.
placeholderPolicy.rule: Placeholders MUST NOT be treated as authored artefacts.

currentRepositoryState.activeSchemaPolicy: Schema files now exist for all 23 entries and are JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 meta-schema valid, so entries are lifecycleState draft. The draft/advisory validator tools/validate-spec/validate-spec.py is CI-enforced for the current corpus but does not activate schemas. No schema may be marked active until the validator posture is formally promoted to active/validator-enforced maturity.
currentRepositoryState.observation: State observed during authoring; no wall-clock timestamp recorded because freshness of governance artefacts is tracked by commit.

governance.valueSourcePolicy: schemaClasses, schemaLifecycleStates, and authorityRole values are drawn only from the vocabulary catalogue. This registry introduces no new vocabulary values and no new taxonomy categories.
rules: Schemas are machine-readable enforcement contracts.
Schemas formalise parts of the ontology; they do NOT replace the ontology.
Schemas MUST align with the taxonomy catalogue.
Schemas MUST use controlled vocabulary values where available.
Schemas MUST NOT duplicate vocabulary enum sets independently without referencing the vocabulary catalogue.
Schema changes can alter semantic meaning and MAY require ADR review.
Schema additions MUST identify the ontology concept they govern.
Schema removals MUST include a disposition.
Schema renames MUST preserve lineage.
Schema IDs MUST be stable.
Generated reports are not schema authority.
../react source files are evidence, not future schema authority.
Source paths from ../react MUST NOT dictate schema paths.
Active schemas MUST exist and be validator-checkable.
Planned schemas MAY be referenced but MUST NOT be enforced as if present.
Schema registry changes MUST be reviewed as semantic-definition changes.
Future AI agents MUST NOT create schemas opportunistically without a registry entry and rationale.

namingConventions.filenameRule: Schema files MUST live under spec/schemas/ and end with .schema.json.
namingConventions.filenameSemantics: Schema filenames MUST use stable semantic names describing the governed concept, not the producing tool.
namingConventions.idRule: Schema IDs MUST use stable semantic IDs and MUST NOT depend on ../react source paths.
namingConventions.idNamespacePolicy: Global, machine-readable artefact IDs MAY use the 'usf.' namespace (e.g. usf.schema-registry, usf.taxonomy-catalog, usf.vocabulary-catalog) because they may be consumed outside the repository context. The 'usf.' namespace on a global artefact ID is NOT a redundant-usf violation. The redundant-usf prohibition applies to repository path segments, package and implementation names, and unnecessary repeated local names and value IDs, never to deliberate globally scoped artefact-ID namespaces.
namingConventions.lifecycleInPathRule: Schema paths MUST NOT encode lifecycle state.
namingConventions.historicalNamesRule: Historical names from ../react MAY appear only as source references, aliases, or quoted evidence; never as canonical schema IDs, paths, or families.
allowedExceptions: the 'usf.' global artefact-ID namespace on machine-readable global identifiers (not a path segment or local value ID)
notAllowed: canonical schema IDs using forbidden terms
canonical schema paths using forbidden terms
canonical schema families using forbidden terms
new target architecture paths using forbidden terms

schemaClasses.aiGuidance: High authority; never weaken governance constraints.

schemaClasses.aiGuidance: Keep raw evidence; never overclaim readiness.

schemaClasses.description: Shapes references to historical/current source evidence and source dispositions.
schemaClasses.validationPurpose: Enforce that every source reference resolves and carries a disposition.

schemaClasses.description: Shapes registries and index/cross-reference artefacts.

schemaClasses.description: Shapes taxonomy catalogues and future taxonomy files.

schemaClasses.description: Shapes vocabulary catalogues and future vocabulary files.

schemaClasses.description: Shapes workflow contracts and cross-capability interactions.

schemaClasses.description: Shapes observability signal definitions.

schemaLifecycleStates.meaning: No longer in use; retained only as lineage.
schemaLifecycleStates.aiGuidance: Do not validate against; disposition required.

schemaLifecycleStates.meaning: Superseded by a specific successor schema.

commonRequirements.note: Requirements every future schema SHOULD follow unless its registry entry records an explicit exception. The common schema is not created here.
conditionalReferences: generated report source references where generated
prohibitions: No silent free-text categories where controlled vocabulary is available.
No schema enum may contradict the vocabulary catalogue.
No schema classification may contradict the taxonomy catalogue.
No schema may treat generated reports as higher authority than raw evidence or semantic definitions.
No schema may permit readiness claims to exceed observed evidence.
No schema may permit hermetic proof to satisfy live external proof unless an explicit semantic rule allows it.
No schema may permit production-shaped to satisfy production-live.
No schema may permit stale or unknown report status to satisfy pass.

commonEnvelope.note: A standard conceptual metadata pattern for governed artefacts. Not every schema requires every field; deviations MUST be explicit in the relevant schema entry. Source-lineage fields are mandatory for artefacts derived from ../react; providerMode and environment are mandatory where evidence/proof/provider claims depend on them.

fields.aiGuidance: Do not overclaim readiness in status.
Never override a higher authority with a lower one.

fields.validatorExpectation: Value from lifecycle-states (or schema-lifecycle-states for schemas).
fields.aiGuidance: Active requires the artefact to exist and be checkable.

fields.validatorExpectation: Resolve each value to a named ontology concept.
Each value contained in taxonomyRefs must resolve to a taxonomy catalogue id; this field may reference any taxonomy defined in the taxonomy catalogue.
Each value contained in vocabularyRefs must resolve to a vocabulary value-set id; this field may reference any value set defined in the vocabulary catalogue.
fields.aiGuidance: Reference value sets; do not duplicate enums.
Behaviour changes need a governing ADR.
Validators enforce; they do not define semantics.

fields.validatorExpectation: Value from provider-modes; hermetic-mock not live.
Value from environment-classes; production-shaped not production-live.

fields.purpose: Source element(s) the artefact derives from.
fields.aiGuidance: Source path does not dictate target path.
No element disappears without a disposition.
Stop or fail on unresolved authority conflict.

rules: Not every schema will require every common envelope field.
Deviations MUST be explicit in the relevant schema entry.
Source lineage fields are mandatory for artefacts derived from ../react.
providerMode and environment are mandatory where evidence/proof/provider claims depend on them.
Generated reports MUST identify the evidence they summarise.
Schema families MUST NOT invent incompatible metadata patterns.

schemaFamilies.purpose: Constitutional and governance artefacts that establish authority and identity.
reactSourceLearnings: ../react treats validators as enforcement, proofs as evidence, code as implementation of canonical semantic artefacts.
schemaFamilies.futureValidatorExpectations: Governance artefacts carry authority and lineage metadata.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: Constitutional docs are currently markdown-governed; a governance schema is deferred. Never weaken constitutional constraints.

schemaFamilies.purpose: Rank-1 semantic contracts and capability semantics.
reactSourceLearnings: ../react v1-capability-closure.json (75 capabilities, 10 facets) and capability-*.json templates ground semantic contracts.
schemaFamilies.futureValidatorExpectations: A capability is proven only when every facet cites authoritative evidence.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: Read semantics before source; never invent a facet.

schemaFamilies.purpose: Classification systems and controlled value sets.
reactSourceLearnings: ../react validator normalises no aliases and fails closed; USF records aliases explicitly so normalisation is controlled.
schemaFamilies.futureValidatorExpectations: Taxonomy classification modes and vocabulary aliases validate against their schemas.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: Taxonomy classifies; vocabulary enumerates; do not collapse them.

reactSourceLearnings: ../react universal-service-foundation-registry.json is data-only and asserts no implementation; registries index, they do not prove.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: Registers before referencing; indexing is not assertion.

schemaFamilies.purpose: References to historical and current source evidence.
reactSourceLearnings: ../react v1-file-inventory.json (~1673 files) and v1-to-v2-path-map.json show every source element must be mapped; nothing disappears without a disposition.
schemaFamilies.futureValidatorExpectations: Every source reference resolves and carries a disposition.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: Classify as evidence before import; never treat source as future authority.

reactSourceLearnings: ../react capability-proof-definition.json (L0-L6; deliveredAndProvenMinimumLevel 3; liveProviderMinimumLevel 4) and the 172 proof-evidence records: emitted evidence preserved through collection; missing evidence fails closed; claimed <= observed.
schemaFamilies.futureValidatorExpectations: Proof fails closed on missing emitted/collected evidence; readiness does not exceed observed evidence.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: Proof is evidence of fact, not a definition of intent.

schemaFamilies.purpose: Provider mode and environment declarations as separate dimensions.
reactSourceLearnings: ../react provider classes and USF_PROVIDER_MODE; e2e profiles split hermetic (internal/identity) from live (external/prod); environment-readiness-gates forbid mocks in prod.
schemaFamilies.futureValidatorExpectations: hermetic-mock cannot satisfy live-external-provider; production-shaped cannot satisfy production-live.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: Never infer a stronger provider mode or environment than the substrate used.

schemaFamilies.purpose: Commands and configuration as governed semantic assets.
reactSourceLearnings: ../react Makefile/make/*.mk, 212 npm scripts incl ~110 proof:* scripts, v2-command-map.json (377 commands), and v1-config-contract-catalogue.json (64 typed keys) show commands/config are semantic assets, not incidental files.
schemaFamilies.futureValidatorExpectations: Commands declare purpose/scope/evidence/failure; config declares secret class and provider/environment/proof relevance.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: Disposition before deleting or renaming a command or config key.

reactSourceLearnings: ../react operational-semantics.json (~235 routes), event-semantics.json (10 events; idempotency/ordering/DLQ/retention), cross-capability-interactions.json (8 interaction types) must become contract-governed, not source-path-governed.
schemaFamilies.futureValidatorExpectations: Interfaces/events have contracts before implementation; runtime drift is detectable.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: Do not infer interfaces or events from code when a contract exists.

schemaFamilies.purpose: Data models, persistence contracts, migrations, and backup/restore.
reactSourceLearnings: ../react data-and-migration-plan.json: PostgreSQL schema-per-tenant, RLS, forward-only checksum-immutable migrations, backup/restore evidence; backup/restore proof must preserve emitted and collected evidence.
schemaFamilies.futureValidatorExpectations: Migrations forward-only and checksum-immutable; tenancy isolation preserved; backup/restore evidence checkable.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: Never edit a committed migration; preserve tenancy invariants.

schemaFamilies.purpose: Observability signals and audit events as semantic assets.
reactSourceLearnings: ../react operational-semantics observabilitySignals/metrics/logs/traces/auditAction; assurance bars 0 routes without tracing/logging/metrics and 0 mutations without audit; Loki/Tempo/Sentry correlation.
schemaFamilies.futureValidatorExpectations: Controlled observability vocabulary; audit required for security-sensitive and state-changing actions.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: Removal of a signal or audit event requires semantic review, not a refactor.

schemaFamilies.purpose: User-facing meaning independent of visual design.
reactSourceLearnings: ../react ui-capability-model.json (28 capabilities, 12 personas) and ui-definition.schema.json; the generator must never read old JSX; UI source is semantic evidence, not final design authority.
schemaFamilies.futureValidatorExpectations: Journeys map to capabilities and proofs; accessibility preserved.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: Visual redesign is not semantic deletion.

reactSourceLearnings: ../react v2-decision-catalog.json (74 accepted) + v2-decision-lineage.json (74 evidence-backed); untraced decisions are rejected (rule R13); a roadmap carries no governance force.
schemaFamilies.futureValidatorExpectations: Every ADR reference resolves; decisions carry invariants, forbidden-drift, and AI-alignment rules.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: ADRs are binding; never generic prose.

reactSourceLearnings: ../react tools/v2-readiness fails closed, normalises no aliases, writes no runtime file, exit codes 0/1/2; reports are reported separately from formal proof so closure is not mistaken for proof.
schemaFamilies.futureValidatorExpectations: unknown/stale never satisfy pass; reports reference evidence and are rank-7.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: Never weaken a rule to pass; never treat a report as canonical.

schemaFamilies.purpose: Controlled import of ../react source elements with explicit disposition.
reactSourceLearnings: ../react file-disposition vocabulary (9 values), command dispositions (carry/merge/retire), test migrationType (4) show every element needs a controlled disposition; bijection rule R10 ensures no silent loss.
schemaFamilies.futureValidatorExpectations: Every imported element has a disposition; import is incomplete without one.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: Disposition every source element; source path does not dictate target path.

schemaFamilies.purpose: AI-agent-relevant artefacts and actions as governed, not informal.
reactSourceLearnings: USF charter section 7, authority-model section 6, standards-profile section 20, ontology sections 14-15 define AI alignment rules, forbidden inferences, and stop conditions.
schemaFamilies.futureValidatorExpectations: AI-generated artefacts carry rationale and references; stop conditions are explicit.
schemaFamilies.aiGuidance: An AI agent holds no authority; stop or fail on unresolved authority conflict.

schemas.title: Schema Registry Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates this schema registry itself.
schemas.requiredBecause: The registry is rank-1 governance and must be self-validating to be externally auditable.
validationResponsibilities: no schema active without a file
driftRisks: Registry drifting from vocabulary/taxonomy.
schemas.aiGuidance: Validate the registry before trusting any schema entry.
deferredDetails: Self-validation wiring (the dialect is resolved as Draft 2020-12 by docs/architecture/schema-authoring-standard.md).

schemas.title: Taxonomy Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates the taxonomy catalogue and future taxonomy files.
schemas.requiredBecause: Taxonomy is rank-1 classification authority and must be shape-validated.
validationResponsibilities: every taxonomy in a known family
driftRisks: Taxonomy categories drifting into vocabulary values.
schemas.aiGuidance: Taxonomy classifies; it does not enumerate controlled values.
deferredDetails: Taxonomy is part of the rank-1 semantic-definition corpus: it is grounded in the ontology concepts Semantic Contract (a normative statement of classification structure) and Registry (a resolution index). The ontology defines no separate Taxonomy concept; these two existing concepts ground it accurately, so no ontology change is required.

schemas.title: Vocabulary Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates the vocabulary catalogue and future vocabulary files.
schemas.requiredBecause: Vocabulary is rank-1 controlled-value authority and must be shape-validated.
validationResponsibilities: every value has lifecycle and AI guidance
driftRisks: Aliases drifting; forbidden values appearing as canonical.
schemas.aiGuidance: Vocabulary is the source of exact allowed values.
deferredDetails: Vocabulary is part of the rank-1 semantic-definition corpus: it is grounded in the ontology concepts Semantic Contract (a normative statement of allowed values) and Registry (a controlled-value index). The ontology defines no separate Vocabulary concept; these two existing concepts ground it accurately, so no ontology change is required.

schemas.title: Semantic Contract Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates semantic contracts (capability facets and other rank-1 contracts).
schemas.requiredBecause: Semantic contracts are the primary authority; they must be complete and evidence-backed.
validationResponsibilities: drop to gap if backing missing
driftRisks: A capability marked proven without facet backing.
schemas.aiGuidance: Read the contract before its implementation; never invent a facet.
deferredDetails: capability-domains value set exists in vocabulary as deferred; canonical values are not yet authored.

schemas.title: Source Reference Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates references to ../react and later source evidence.
schemas.requiredBecause: Lineage must be traceable and resolvable.
validationResponsibilities: reference resolves to a real path/commit
driftRisks: Broken or fabricated lineage.
schemas.aiGuidance: Cite lineage; never treat the reference as live authority.

schemas.title: Source Disposition Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates the treatment of imported, deferred, transformed, rejected, or retired source elements.
schemas.requiredBecause: No source element may disappear without a disposition.
driftRisks: Silent source loss.
schemas.aiGuidance: Disposition is a recorded decision, not silence; it does not imply implementation acceptance.
deferredDetails: Whether regenerate and promote-to-conformance warrant distinct canonical disposition values.

schemas.title: Evidence Envelope Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates the common evidence envelope across evidence kinds.
schemas.requiredBecause: Evidence must be typed, source-referenced, and freshness-checkable.
validationResponsibilities: provider mode and environment where relevant
driftRisks: Hiding missing raw evidence behind a report.
schemas.aiGuidance: Never conflate kinds; missing evidence fails closed.

schemas.title: Proof Evidence Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates proof claim, execution, emitted evidence, collected evidence, provider mode, environment, and readiness claim consistency.
schemas.requiredBecause: Proof must be honest: claimed level <= observed; missing evidence fails closed.
validationResponsibilities: fail closed on missing emitted/collected evidence
driftRisks: Overclaiming proof level; relabelling hermetic as live.
schemas.aiGuidance: Proof level is not readiness status; never relabel upward.
deferredDetails: Exact proof evidence schema; proof-level vocabulary finalisation.

schemas.title: Provider Mode Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates provider mode declarations and prevents hermetic/live confusion.
schemas.requiredBecause: Provider mode is proof-relevant and must be explicit and honest.
validationResponsibilities: adapter identifies port and provider mode
driftRisks: Mislabelling hermetic as live.
schemas.aiGuidance: mock IdP is valid hermetic proof but never live external proof.
deferredDetails: Whether to add a no-provider value for non-runtime capabilities.

schemas.title: Environment Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates environment class declarations and prevents production-shaped/production-live confusion.
schemas.requiredBecause: Environment is proof-relevant and must be explicit.
validationResponsibilities: environment does not upgrade provider mode
driftRisks: Treating an environment name as a readiness claim.
schemas.aiGuidance: Keep environment distinct from provider mode.
deferredDetails: Confirm exact historical stage-to-class mapping during import.

schemas.title: Command Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates Make targets, package scripts, CLI commands, validation/proof/import/build/runtime/report-generation commands.
schemas.requiredBecause: Commands are semantic assets, not incidental scripts.
driftRisks: Silent command loss/rename.
schemas.aiGuidance: Disposition before deleting or renaming a command.

schemas.title: Configuration Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates env vars, config files, config keys, secret-bearing settings, provider/environment/proof/runtime/compose configuration.
schemas.requiredBecause: Configuration is a governed semantic asset; secret handling must be explicit.
driftRisks: Hand-editing generated config; misclassifying a secret.
schemas.aiGuidance: Regenerate from manifests; never leak secret values.

schemas.title: Interface Contract Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates API routes, commands, queries, event handlers, service boundaries, CLI interfaces, provider ports, adapter interfaces, internal and external contracts.
schemas.requiredBecause: Interfaces must be contract-first or contract-reconciled, not implementation-guessed.
driftRisks: Inferring an interface from handlers.
schemas.aiGuidance: Define or reconcile the contract first.

schemas.title: Event Contract Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates event/message contracts and event semantics.
schemas.requiredBecause: Events must have contracts (schema, idempotency, ordering, DLQ, retention) before emission.
driftRisks: Inventing events in code.
schemas.aiGuidance: Define the event contract before emitting an event.

schemas.title: Workflow Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates workflows, cross-capability interactions, state transitions, async/sync operations, failure paths, and compensation paths.
schemas.requiredBecause: Workflow ordering, consistency, and compensation are contract-level semantics.
driftRisks: Losing compensation/ordering semantics in a refactor.
schemas.aiGuidance: Declare compensation and failure paths explicitly.

schemas.title: Data and Migration Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates data models, persistence contracts, identifiers, relationships, migrations, seed data, fixtures, backup evidence, restore evidence, and retention/deletion concerns.
schemas.requiredBecause: Migrations are forward-only and checksum-immutable; tenancy isolation must be preserved; backup/restore evidence must be preserved. Classed as semantic-schema because data models, migrations, and backup/restore are rank-1 semantic contracts (data semantics), which the semantic-schema class explicitly covers; no dedicated data-schema vocabulary class is needed.
sourceInputs: ../react data-and-migration-plan.json (schema-per-tenant; RLS; migration chain 001..034 then 035+; backupRestore; destructiveOpControls)
driftRisks: Editing a committed migration; tenant data leakage.
schemas.aiGuidance: Never edit a committed migration; preserve tenancy invariants.

schemas.title: Observability Signal Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates logs, metrics, traces, spans, runtime events, runtime proof outputs, service/resource attributes, and correlation identifiers.
schemas.requiredBecause: Observability is a semantic asset that supports proof, debugging, and drift detection.
driftRisks: Removing a signal as a refactor.
schemas.aiGuidance: Removal requires semantic review.

schemas.title: Audit Event Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates audit events, security-sensitive audits, state-changing audits, and accountability records.
schemas.requiredBecause: Audit is required for security-sensitive and state-changing operations.
driftRisks: Removing an audit event as a refactor.
schemas.aiGuidance: Every mutating/privileged action needs a defined audit semantic.

schemas.title: UI Semantic Model Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates UI surfaces, pages, journeys, states, validation, errors, permissions, accessibility concerns, user actions, command/query mappings, and e2e proof mappings.
schemas.requiredBecause: UI behaviour and proof expectations must be preserved so the visual layer can be regenerated without inventing behaviour.
validationResponsibilities: journeys map to capabilities and proofs
driftRisks: Treating a UI component as a capability; deleting a journey as a restyle.
schemas.aiGuidance: Visual redesign is not semantic deletion; derive from behaviour, not JSX.

schemas.title: ADR Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates ADR structure: semantic refs, source refs, proof refs, validator refs, invariants, permitted changes, forbidden drift, consequences, and AI-alignment rules.
schemas.requiredBecause: ADRs are rank-2 binding decisions and must be traceable, not generic prose.
driftRisks: Untraced or prose-only decisions.
schemas.aiGuidance: ADRs are binding; record decisions as ADRs with references.

schemas.title: Validator Report Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates validator report shape: severities, statuses, stale/unknown/pass distinctions, evidence references, and blocking/advisory findings.
schemas.requiredBecause: Reports are rank-7; unknown/stale must never satisfy pass and reports must reference evidence.
sourceInputs: ../react tools/v2-readiness finding shape {ruleId, severity, subject, message}; exit codes 0/1/2
driftRisks: Believing a stale report; downgrading blocking to advisory.
schemas.aiGuidance: Never treat a report as canonical; regenerate from current state.

schemas.title: Import Manifest Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates controlled import manifests from ../react.
schemas.requiredBecause: Imports must be complete and traceable; no source element disappears without a disposition.
driftRisks: Silent source loss; source path dictating target path.
schemas.aiGuidance: Source path does not dictate target schema/path; disposition every element.
deferredDetails: Exact source import manifest mapping from ../react.

schemas.title: AI Governance Schema
schemas.purpose: Validates AI instructions, AI-generated artefacts, AI-reviewed artefacts, AI alignment rules, forbidden inferences, authority conflicts, drift risks, and required stop conditions.
schemas.requiredBecause: AI work is governed, not informal; AI agents hold no authority.
driftRisks: Treating AI output as authoritative without checks.
schemas.aiGuidance: Stop or fail on unresolved authority conflict; never self-grant authority.

externalStandards.affectsSchemas: JSON Schema is the mechanism for validating all USF JSON artefacts; every schema is a JSON Schema with explicit $schema and $id.
externalStandards.willNotClaimYet: Active/validator-enforced maturity is not yet reached; a draft/advisory validator (jsonschema==4.10.3) now exists and is CI-enforced for the corpus (see schema-authoring §26 Amendment A). The Draft 2020-12 dialect is resolved by docs/architecture/schema-authoring-standard.md (https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema).
externalStandards.validatorImplications: Validators run JSON Schema validation and fail closed on invalidity.
externalStandards.aiGuidance: Validate generated JSON against its schema before claiming completion.

externalStandards.affectsSchemas: Normative language governs human-readable standards and ADRs; it does not by itself define JSON shape.
externalStandards.willNotClaimYet: No claim that uppercase keywords define machine validation.
externalStandards.validatorImplications: Optional keyword-usage lint for normative documents.

reactSourceLearnings.learning: Source files are semantic evidence.
Make targets are semantic command evidence.
Package scripts are command evidence.
Env/config files are configuration evidence.
Compose services are runtime/environment/provider/configuration evidence.
Tests and e2e journeys are behavioural/UI/proof evidence where applicable.
Proof scripts are separate from generated reports.
Generated reports are lower authority than raw evidence and semantic artefacts.
Readiness claims must not exceed observed evidence.
Emitted proof evidence must be preserved through collection and reporting.
Missing collected evidence must fail closed.
Provider mode must be explicit.
Environment must be explicit.
Production-shaped is not production-live.
Hermetic mock proof is valid for internal proof but not live external proof.
No source element should disappear without disposition.
Source path does not dictate target schema path.
Generated readiness summaries must remain traceable to underlying evidence.
UI source is semantic evidence but not necessarily future design authority.
Operational semantics, event semantics, and cross-capability interactions must become contract-governed rather than source-path-governed.
Backup/restore evidence requires explicit schema support because proof claims must preserve emitted and collected evidence.
Commands/configuration from Makefile, package scripts, env files, config directories, and compose files must be treated as semantic assets.
Validators must fail closed on missing evidence rather than silently downgrading or passing claims.

validationExpectations: Registry file must parse as JSON.
Schema entry IDs must be unique.
Schema paths must be unique.
Schema IDs and paths must follow naming rules (no forbidden canonical terms).
Lifecycle states must exist in the vocabulary catalogue schema-lifecycle-states value set.
Schema classes must exist in the vocabulary catalogue schema-classes value set.
Schema families must be known in this registry.
Taxonomy references must resolve to taxonomy catalogue entries where possible.
Vocabulary references must resolve to vocabulary catalogue value sets where possible.
Required common metadata must be present.
Schema entries must identify governed ontology concepts.
Schema entries must not reference forbidden path names.
Planned schemas may be referenced as planned, but active schemas must exist and be validator-checkable.
Generated reports must reference evidence.
Evidence schemas must require provider mode and environment where relevant.
Proof schemas must fail closed on missing emitted/collected evidence.
Import schemas must require source disposition.
Provider-mode schema must prevent hermetic-mock from satisfying live-external-provider claims.
Environment schema must prevent production-shaped from satisfying production-live claims.
Validator-report schema must prevent unknown or stale from satisfying pass.
Schema registry validation must eventually check itself with schema-registry.schema.json.
aiAgentRules: Read charter, authority model, standards profile, ontology, taxonomy, vocabulary, and this schema registry before creating schemas.
Do not create schema files without a registry entry.
Do not create schema fields without an ontology concept or rationale.
Use taxonomy categories where classification is needed.
Use vocabulary values where exact allowed values are needed.
Never infer schema authority from source structure alone.
Never treat generated reports as canonical schema input.
Never upgrade hermetic mock evidence into live external evidence.
Never treat stale or unknown as pass.
Do not mark a schema active unless the file exists and validators can check it.
Fail or stop when a schema/ontology/taxonomy/vocabulary conflict is unresolved.
Do not create implementation directories or runtime code as part of schema registry work.
